messages:
maria: Heads-up — thinking about a new 'edge hedging' policy for hosted API routing. Goal: prioritize region-affinity but allow tiered hedging to cheaper model variants during regional pressure. Sketch below, want feedback.

jake: love the name :smile: quick Q — what's considered 'pressure'? 95th p99 latency? or backend error rate?

maria: both. probe signals: p50/p95/p99 tail, error rate, queue length, and token processing time. If any > threshold for X seconds then trigger hedging.

vikram: do we have per-tenant thresholds? enterprise vs free? should be per-customer tier yes.

maria: yes — plan: tier map: premium -> strict latency SLO (low tolerance), standard -> moderate, trial/free -> aggressive hedging to cheaper variants. Also ROI calc for cost delta per fallback step.

anya: how about model variant fallback ordering? degrade quality gracefully: same-family quantized -> smaller model -> cross-region full model only when necessary. Also prefer variants validated by evals for that tenant's prompts.

ben: sketch config prototype:

```
route_policy:
  affinity: region
  probes: [latency, errors, queue]
  thresholds:
    premium: {p99_ms: 250, errors_pct: 0.5}
    standard: {p99_ms: 600, errors_pct: 1}
    trial: {p99_ms: 900, errors_pct: 2}
  fallback_order:
    - model-x-8q
    - model-x-4q
    - model-small
    - cross-region-full
  hedging_window_s: 10
  hysteresis: {consecutive_windows: 2, cooldown_s: 30}
```

nora: console UX note — operators need to see 'why' we routed away: show probe that triggered + snapshot of model variant used + cost delta estimate. Also allow manual override per-tenant and a 'snooze hedging' toggle.

maria: agree. telemetry: emit event 'route_decision' with fields [tenant_id, tier, origin_region, execution_region, probe_vector, fallback_step, cost_delta_est, trace_id]. Keep payload compact (no large prompt blobs).

jake: what about quota counting when routing cross-region? ensure tokens billed to tenant's billing region or at least annotate billing with origin_region vs execution_region so finance can reconcile.

enums-bot: note: route-service schema v2 will add 'execution_region' field — plan to ship with telemetry change.

ben: canary plan: route-service v3.2 -> 5% traffic, synthetic degraded region test to validate hedging triggers. precheck: math on average cost increase if many fallbacks go cross-region.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: route-service v3.2 canary at 1704123600 (5% traffic)

vikram: canary + synthetic traffic to simulate degraded region. Also need hysteresis to avoid oscillation between two regions. add probe scoring smoothing (exponential moving avg).

anya: hysteresis idea: require 2 consecutive probe windows beyond threshold and cooldown 30s after fallback. Also track a 'revert_score' if quality regressions spike after fallback.

ben: thought: tenant-level circuit-breaker to stop hedging for a tenant that sees automated-quality-regression post-fallback. Auto-rollback to original region for that tenant for X minutes and flag for SRE review.

maria: sounds good. action items:
- ben: add config schema + patch for fallback_order/hysteresis
- jake: telemetry event spec + dashboards for route_decision and hedging_rate by tier
- nora: console mockups for routing trace + manual override UI
- vikram: canary plan + synthetic tests + EMAs in probe service

maria: ping me in #eng-oncall when canary starts. thanks

deploy-bot: canary started for route-service v3.2 (5% traffic) — 1704123600

jake: quick followup — do we want to expose per-route (completions vs embeddings vs rerank) policies? embeddings are heavier and have different latency/cost profile; maybe stricter affinity for embeddings.

maria: yes, allow per-workload overrides. keep sensible defaults per-tier and per-workload.

nora: UI: filter by route type and tenant, show last 1h decisions with a tiny sparkline for p99 and an explanation crumb for the latest fallback. Add link to trace/trace_id.

jake: ok i'll mock dashboards and open PR for event schema. I'll include a CostImpact dashboard that shows estimated vs actual.

maria: wrapped up. thanks all :pray:
